answer: Behavioral timing fingerprinting scores each new identity against population baselines for action latency and session rhythm, flagging near-duplicate profiles for retroactive review. A sybil cluster leaves a detectable delta in inter-arrival variance that individual cloaking rarely hides. Every flagged identity must then pass a costly challenge-response sequence whose failure echo propagates across its suspected cluster, freezing linked accounts. Honest users post a small quartz of verification effort once, while attackers pay that cost multiplied across every clone they operate.
